value.deck: GitHub now offers a new tool that helps teams easily check if all their software development rules are being followed across many projects, making sure everything runs smoothly.
shortVersion: Imagine you're building a big LEGO castle with many friends. You all agree on rules, like "only blue bricks for the roof." This new tool helps the leader quickly see if everyone is actually using blue bricks for all the castle parts. It's like a central dashboard for leaders to check if all the agreed-upon rules for building software are being followed across many different projects at once.

This new feature, called "Rule Insights," shows them which rules are working, which ones people are accidentally skipping, and if any rules are clashing with each other. Before, they had to check each project individually, which was like checking every single LEGO piece. Now, they get one clear overview.
This makes it much easier for big teams to keep their software projects organized and secure. It helps them quickly fix problems and ensure everyone is building software the right way.
value.plainLanguage: GitHub has a new tool that helps big teams easily see and manage all the rules for building their software across many projects.

keyTerms.meaning: A popular online platform where people store, manage, and share the code for their software projects.
Think of this as a folder or a dedicated space on GitHub where all the files and history for one specific software project are kept.
These are like special rules set up for a part of a software project (a 'branch') to make sure important changes are reviewed and approved before they become part of the main project.
This means the new tool can look at all the projects (repositories) that belong to a large company or group (an 'organization') on GitHub, not just one project at a time.

value.whyItMatters: Imagine a big company that builds many different software apps. They need to make sure all their apps are built safely and consistently. This new tool helps the people in charge quickly check if all the rules are being followed across all those different apps, saving a lot of time and preventing mistakes. It's like having a master checklist for all your projects.
